text: Before consolidating anything, Mara inventories what already exists. Skipping that step would just carry every orphaned account and inconsistency forward, hidden behind a federation layer instead of visible in two separate consoles.

Querying Hartwell's Entra ID tenant through the Microsoft Graph API turns up about 1,400 user accounts, including disabled-but-never-deleted logins, roughly 85 overlapping security groups with names that don't describe what they grant, and dozens of service principals, several scoped far wider than the one task they were created for.

On the AWS side, three separate accounts under one Organization each grew their own IAM users and roles independently. A simple boto3 script pulls every user with the list_users paginator, pulls their access keys, and flags any active key older than 180 days. Across all three accounts, dozens of users are still authenticating with exactly that kind of long-lived, unrotated credential.

The real finding isn't any single bad account. It's that Hartwell has no single system of record for identity: answering who can access what means checking four different places with nothing keeping them in sync. Next lesson turns that finding into a target architecture.
